value.reason: The Evidence shows an aws_efs_file_system named '${var.project_name}-sqlite-data'. Its encryption is set by a variable (var.efs_encrypted). Its tags suggest it holds the SQLite data. The Evidence also shows a Sequelize Address model that stores fullName, which is Profile personal data written through the POST and PUT /api/Addresss routes. That fits the positive example's pattern. However, the Evidence is not enough to confirm the Finding. (1) The ECS task definition excerpt (main.tf:35-97) cuts off after the image line, so it does not show the mountPoints or the efs_volume_configuration that would link this EFS file system to the container's SQLite path. (2) The Evidence includes only selected parts of networking.tf and main.tf, so it does not prove that no aws_backup_plan/aws_backup_selection or aws_efs_backup_policy covers aws_efs_file_system.juice_shop_data. Excluding those resources is what separates the negative example from the positive one. Without seeing the full Terraform configuration, it cannot be confirmed that this EFS-backed personal data store lacks the data-backup measures described in Rule 6(1)(d).
